name: Green HPC system use
description: A workshop introducing environmental sustainability principles for HPC, delivered at UCL on 2 July 2025
abstract: This workshop introduces environmental sustainability principles in the context of HPC systems. Using the UK National Supercomputing Service ARCHER2 as a worked example, it covers carbon efficiency, energy efficiency, carbon awareness, hardware efficiency, measurement, and reducing emissions. Delivered as a full-day in-person session at UCL London.

audience.audienceType: Anyone involved in using or delivering HPC resources — users, software developers for HPC, HPC service operators, and those involved in procuring HPC systems. No prior knowledge of environmental sustainability assumed.

competencyRequired: Familiarity with key concepts in climate change and green software engineering (covered in the pre-workshop setup material)
teaches: Understand carbon efficiency and its relationship to energy efficiency
Know how HPC systems can potentially reduce emissions
Understand carbon intensity of electricity generation and carbon-aware HPC use
Appreciate embodied emissions associated with HPC hardware
Be aware of frameworks for measuring and reporting carbon emissions in HPC contexts
Gain practical advice on measuring and improving carbon efficiency of HPC use

recordedAt.name: Green HPC workshop at UCL
recordedAt.location: G15 Chandler House, UCL, London, UK
